entry_state: The implementation specifies one transactional owner, immutable evidence and views, complete request fingerprints and independent result statuses. Corrections follow candidate-set dependencies without rewriting old selections. Durability, checkpoints and migrations have observable requirements, while the plugin interface must expose all material numerical inputs and preserve unknown solver outcomes.
exit_state: Review decisions preserve source history, and identity distinguishes evidence, model and run changes. Adapter examples show why successful conversion can lose context, omit pages or duplicate numeric transformations. Source-byte identity, visible readings, structural checks and execution validation remain separate; the inline-value subsection continues on the next page.
findings: Reviewing an extraction does not accept its accounting treatment; model confidence is not economic probability.
A PDF can retain hidden text that agrees across extractors but differs from the visible title.
Page counts, partial-success status, requested OCR and model names do not by themselves establish completed extraction or pinned model identity.
Table syntax does not ensure rectangular nonoverlapping cells, and parsed numeric values may already include scale and sign. No new confirmed manuscript defect.

chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:4.open_question: What must an external plugin disclose?
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:4.parent_contribution: It enumerates contract, behavior, measurement, report and solver inputs.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:4.belief_update: Hidden dates, caches or random state can change results across branches.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:4.removal_verdict: Removal would leave external calculators outside reproducibility rules.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:4.swap_verdict: It follows storage guarantees before human review.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:4.entry_verdict: Version, types, information dates and numerical measure are explicit.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:4.exit_verdict: Unknown solver outcomes preserve unresolved coverage.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:4.promise_verdict: A witness establishes existence, not family completeness.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:4.distinct_contribution_verdict: It ties external computation to the same evidence and status discipline.

chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:5.entry_belief: Plugins and extractors can propose typed outputs.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:5.open_question: How does a reviewer assess a coherent disclosure?
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:5.parent_contribution: It places source, context and reconciliation beside the proposal.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:5.belief_update: Deterministic validity does not establish evidentiary acceptance.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:5.exit_question: How are failures and reruns recorded?
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:5.removal_verdict: Removal would allow generated interpretations to enter as accepted facts.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:5.swap_verdict: It follows plugins before operational recovery.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:5.entry_verdict: Review actions have explicit reasons and structured effects.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:5.exit_verdict: The initial local interface stays proportionate to research use.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:5.promise_verdict: Token confidence is never automatically a weight over histories.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:5.distinct_contribution_verdict: It gives review a substantive disclosure unit rather than an isolated number.

chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:6.entry_belief: Review and execution require stable evidence.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:6.open_question: What permits a restart to reproduce the same work?
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:6.parent_contribution: It requires atomic progress and a run manifest.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:6.belief_update: A missing Git revision must be recorded honestly with content hashes.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:6.exit_question: How do changed decisions affect descendants?
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:6.removal_verdict: Removal would leave reruns detached from their inputs.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:6.swap_verdict: It precedes decision invalidation and identity detail.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:6.entry_verdict: Extraction and simulation have distinct restart conditions.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:6.exit_verdict: The manifest identifies source, settings and environment.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:6.distinct_contribution_verdict: It specifies recovery provenance without inventing a commit.

chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:7.open_question: How does correction preserve earlier meaning?
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:7.parent_contribution: It distinguishes acceptance, alternatives, rejection and supersession.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:7.belief_update: Correcting OCR differs from an issuer changing its reported assertion.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:7.removal_verdict: Removal would let a new reading silently rewrite old journals.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:7.swap_verdict: It follows review workflow before identity rules.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:7.entry_verdict: Acceptance is explicitly scoped to the reviewed layer.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:7.exit_verdict: Frozen results retain original decisions and are stale only for current use.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:7.promise_verdict: The 720-to-120 extraction correction differs from the 120-to-110 issuer revision.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:7.distinct_contribution_verdict: It gives review actions concrete effects on downstream work.

chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:8.entry_belief: Corrections can change evidence without changing economics.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:8.open_question: Which identity must survive or change?
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:8.parent_contribution: It separates evidence, model and run closures and stable event keys.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:8.belief_update: Harmless ordering and branch enumeration must not change event effects or random coupling.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:8.exit_question: How do adapters exchange these meanings?
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:8.removal_verdict: Removal would undermine replay and exact request conflict handling.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:8.swap_verdict: It follows revision semantics before typed exchanges.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:8.entry_verdict: Serialization conventions and legacy scope are explicit.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:8.exit_verdict: Migration retains old bytes and one mutable owner per transition.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:8.promise_verdict: The illustrative hash-to-uniform mapping is not promoted to a production generator.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:8.distinct_contribution_verdict: It distinguishes identity invariance from arbitrary economic equivalence.

chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:9.entry_belief: Portable identity and request rules are defined.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:9.open_question: What does each selected adapter exchange?
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:9.parent_contribution: It connects named tools to typed records and retained diagnostic causes.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:9.belief_update: Source interfaces support designs without establishing completed adapters.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:9.exit_question: How can a successful extraction still lose a fact?
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:9.removal_verdict: Removal would leave component reuse unconnected to semantics.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:9.swap_verdict: It follows identities and precedes concrete extraction failures.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:9.entry_verdict: Historical Core 0 examples require an explicit decoder relation.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:9.exit_verdict: Pinned release and licence evidence remain part of integration acceptance.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:9.promise_verdict: The source-grounded boundaries distinguish Z3 checks from other unexecuted adapters.
chapters/09-implementation.tex:section:9.distinct_contribution_verdict: It identifies each component responsibility without delegating accounting meaning to it.
